'''Fudbalski klub Željezničar Sarajevo''' ([[English language|English]]: Football Club Željezničar Sarajevo), commonly referred to as '''Željo''', is a professional [[Association football|football]] club, based in [[Sarajevo]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]]. The name ''Željezničar'' means "railway worker", originating from their establishment by a group of railway workers in 1921. Throughout its history, the club has cultivated a reputation for producing talented home-grown players through its youth school.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://fkzeljeznicar.ba/berjan-zeljo-je-dobijao-aplauz-po-cijeloj-jugoslaviji/6975/ | title= Berjan: Željo nije dobijao aplauz po cijeloj Jugoslaviji nikad| publisher=fkzeljeznicar.ba | access-date=19 August 2015}}</ref>

During the days of [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|socialist Yugoslavia]], FK Željezničar were national champions in the [[1971–72 Yugoslav First League|1971–72 season]], qualifying for the [[European Cup]] during the [[1972–73 European Cup|1972–73 season]]. The club has also finished as [[1970–71 Yugoslav First League|runners-up]] once in the league, and contested the [[1980–81 Yugoslav Cup]] final. In Europe, the club reached the [[UEFA Cup]] quarter-finals during the [[1971–72 UEFA Cup|1971–72 season]] and the semi-finals during the [[1984–85 UEFA Cup|1984–85 season]]. The latter remains the most successful European campaign by any club from Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Alongside [[FK Sarajevo]], Željezničar is the most successful football team from Bosnia and Herzegovina, having won six [[Premier League of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnian championships]], six [[Bosnia and Herzegovina Football Cup|Bosnian Cup]]s and three [[Supercup of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnian Supercup]]s, in addition to the [[Yugoslav First League]] title in 1972. The club's so far best post-[[Bosnian War|war]] European result was qualifying to the [[2002–03 UEFA Champions League#Third qualifying round|2002–03 Champions League third qualifying round]], losing to [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]. Their biggest rival is FK Sarajevo with whom they contest the biggest football match in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the [[Sarajevo derby]]."}}
